summary.headline: Deep Industries Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 49% YoY to INR248.7 crores, but a INR208 crore Kandla receivable write-off drove the reported loss.
summary.overview: Q4 operating revenue grew 49% YoY to INR248.7 crores and FY26 revenue rose 55% to INR891 crores, with Q4 EBITDA up 71% to INR106.85 crores at a 39% margin. Management wrote off about INR208 crores of legacy Kandla Energy trade receivables as an exceptional, non-cash item, while keeping roughly INR160 crores of Dolphin Group receivables on the books based on arbitration awards. A gas leak at Mori-5 well (Andhra Pradesh) in January 2026 delayed production enhancement by 5 to 6 months, and the company dropped its QIP plan.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 net profit excl. exceptional item (net of tax)
FY26 net profit excl. exceptional item (net of tax)
FY26 net cash from operating activities
Exceptional item: Kandla legacy receivables write-off

segments.name: Drilling rigs / workover
segments.commentary: Rig fleet is 100% utilised, so new orders need new rig capex. Three new workover rigs (100 and 150 ton) mobilised in Q4 are expected to add over INR1.5 crores a month combined.

segments.name: Gas processing
segments.commentary: Around 12% to 15% spare capacity in the existing fleet. A tender already bid is expected to need about INR150 crores of capex if awarded.

segments.name: Dolphin Offshore
segments.commentary: Single offshore asset. Q4 revenue rose from INR30 crores to INR45 crores, but EBITDA fell from INR22 crores to INR12 crores, including about INR10 crores of one-off expected credit loss provision. Management guides about INR150 crores revenue in FY27 at roughly 60% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Production enhancement (PEC)
segments.commentary: Mori-5 well was shut under a pollution board stop-production order after the January 2026 gas leak. Other wells remain producing and selling gas. Management expects a 1 to 2 quarter delay, and the Mori-5 contract is cited at INR120 crores to INR150 crores run-rate once restored.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25% to 30% YoY, implying about INR950 crores to INR1,100 crores; management said this is achievable.
EBITDA margin expected to hold around 44% to 45% year on year, varying 1% to 2%.
FY28 profit of INR450 crores to INR500 crores was discussed by an analyst; management said it saw no issue with the growth trajectory but did not confirm the figure.
Capex of around INR300 crores targeted for FY27: about INR150 crores under PEC and about INR150 crores for rigs and gas processing. Offshore fleet additions could raise this.
A 2,000 HP drilling rig, if secured, needs capex of about INR100 crores to INR120 crores, funded by internal accruals and debt. Bids are being pursued through a JV.
Management expects over INR800 crores of the INR3,000 crore order book to execute in FY27; the rest depends on new orders expected in the next few months.
capex_capacity: Rig segment fully utilised; new rig capex needed for any new contract.
Gas processing has about 12% to 15% spare capacity before capex is needed.
Planned FY27 capex of about INR300 crores, including about INR150 crores under PEC and about INR150 crores for rigs and gas processing.
Targeted ROI on new capex is more than 20%, per management.
Offshore fleet expansion is planned, one asset at a time, with selective bidding.
demand_pricing: Order book has held at around INR3,000 crores for four to five quarters; management says PEC orders and new higher-capacity rig opportunities should lift it in a quarter or two.
Bid pipeline of INR500 crores to INR600 crores covers submitted bids only and excludes PEC; a new PEC tender (15-year) was received last week and is being evaluated.
Single-client dependence reduced to below 40% of operating revenue.
Services business has no seasonality (24/7 operations), so Q1 is expected to resemble Q4.
PEC contracts use a free gas price mechanism, so higher gas prices can lift PEC order values; services demand benefits from sentiment.
Company does not hedge USD receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Are all legacy receivables written off, and why are Dolphin receivables still on the books?
qa_highlights.answer: All Kandla legacy receivables were written off. INR160 crores of Dolphin Group receivables are retained because of arbitration awards in the company's favour and the client relationship; management is optimistic of recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dolphin Q4 margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a one-off ECL provision of about INR10 crores and a gross-rather-than-net billing opportunity that raised revenue and expenses. It said year-on-year comparison is more appropriate than quarterly, given repair cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Mori-5 stop-production order material?
qa_highlights.answer: The order applies only to that well. Other wells are producing and gas is being sold; restoring Mori-5 needs equipment hire, expected to take 1 to 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company bid for 2,000 HP rigs, and does it have a pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, through a JV. The bid pipeline is about INR500 crores to INR600 crores, and management is confident of qualifying.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the outlook for PEC and order flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PEC orders are arriving steadily and that higher-capacity rig opportunities should lift the order book above current levels in a quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: Is the QIP still going ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it has decided not to proceed with the QIP given improved cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company bid for the Gamij and Geleki PEC fields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has the financial capacity, but the bidding strategy depends on completing geological studies and the work programme.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR3,000 crore order book reconcile with 25% to 30% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap would come from new orders (2 to 3 major contracts expected in roughly the next month) that would be mobilised within the first six months.

risks_watch: Mori-5 well shutdown and the 1 to 2 quarter PEC delay could affect the PEC revenue run-rate.
About INR160 crores of Dolphin Group receivables remain on the balance sheet pending arbitration, and recovery is not yet assured.
Order book has been flat at about INR3,000 crores for four to five quarters; FY27 growth depends on new order inflows.
Dolphin Offshore margins are volatile and depend on repair and breakdown costs; the single-asset model adds concentration risk.
Rig damage incident and force majeure status for a workover rig are still under consideration, with the company's participation in new workover contracts uncertain.
Green hydrogen MOU with Advait Green Energy is at an early stage; no timeline or size yet disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order flow, but cautious and vague on specific timelines for PEC restoration, order inflow and new bids. Management was clear on write-off and capex figures, and deflected on the Mori-5 stop order, the rig incident and Dolphin's quarterly margin.
key_quotes: Our order book remains robust, revolving consistently over INR3,000 crores, providing multiyear revenue visibility and reinforcing confidence in our long-term growth outlook.
This nonrecurring and noncash adjustment reflects our commitment to financial discipline.
So we have decided not to go ahead with QIP.
